rules.quote: Write the name of the organisation the same way the organisation writes it.
rules.specification: Follow the official spelling, punctuation, logograms, and capitalization used by the organisation, except if the name is entirely lower case, in which case use an initial capital in body text. Preserve medial capitals (e.g. eBay, eSafety) even at sentence start.
rules.violation_condition: an organisation name written with spelling, punctuation, capitalization or logograms differing from how the organisation writes its own name (except when written entirely in lower case)
when: If the organisation name is in all lower case, use an initial capital in body text.
If the name starts with a lower case letter but has a medial capital (such as eBay or eSafety), write it with the medial capital, including at the beginning of a sentence.
In registered business names that appear in all capitals, use the capitalization style preferred by the organisation on its website and publications.
rules.why: G-1, G-2, G-4: The main instruction covers the casing, logograms, and exceptions (all-caps ABN entries, medial caps, all-lower-case names).

rules.quote: If you cite a source written by an organisation that has since changed its name, use the name that was published in the source.
rules.violation_condition: citing a source written by an organisation using its current name instead of the name published in the source
when: When citing a source published under a former name of an organisation.
rules.why: Specific rule governing citation of past organisation names.

covers.quote: Shortened forms of the name

rules.quote: Use the organisation’s shortened form only if the organisation regularly uses it in its own content.
rules.specification: Only use shortened forms or initialisms endorsed or regularly used by the organisation itself (e.g. 'Home Affairs' rather than 'DHA').
rules.violation_condition: using an unauthorised or unofficial shortened form (or initialism) for an organisation that does not regularly use it in its own content
rules.why: Specific rule prohibiting arbitrary or unendorsed shortened forms.

rules.quote: Spell out the shortened form the first time, unless the organisation’s name is known only by the shortened form.
rules.violation_condition: introducing a shortened form of an organisation's name on first mention without spelling out the full name first (unless known only by the shortened form), or conversely spelling out a name known only by its acronym
when: Unless the organisation's name is known only by the shortened form (e.g. IKEA).
rules.why: Standard rule for first mention of shortened forms with explicit positive and negative examples.

when: Except when the abbreviation finishes a sentence.
rules.why: Explicit punctuation instruction for corporate designator abbreviations.

covers.quote:
Use initial capitals for:

* all words capitalised in the full, official names of organisations
* the first mention of an organisation.
generic terms – such as ‘the department’or ‘the agency’ – even if the organisation being referenced capitalises the generic term in its content
mentions of several organisations with the same generic name.

parts.quote: Australian Academy of the Humanities – the academy
Department of Finance – the department

examples.note: Plural generic term uses lower case.

parts.quote: The departments of Health and Finance – the departments
Western Sydney University – the university
Australian Ballet Company – the company
Royal Commission into Misconduct in the Banking, Superannuation and Financial Services Industry – the royal commission
Gundagai Shire Council – the shire council/the council
Regional Australia Summit – the summit

rules.quote:
Don’t use an initial capital for:

* generic terms – such as ‘the department’or ‘the agency’ – even if the organisation being referenced capitalises the generic term in its content
* mentions of several organisations with the same generic name.
rules.violation_condition: capitalising a generic term referring to an organisation (such as 'the Department', 'the Agency', or 'the departments')
rules.why: G-1, G-2: Specific prohibition against capitalising generic organisation references.

covers.quote: In body text, use lower case for the definite article in the names of organisations

Some organisations use the definite article ‘The’ in their name with an initial capital. Use the full name, including ‘The’, in 2 situations:

* in emails and letters
* if the name appears in an alphabetical list (arrange by ‘The’ as the first word in the name).
If organisations omit the definite article from their name, don’t use it in emails and letters. In body text, ‘the’ appears before the correct name or isn’t needed at all.

parts.quote: Next year the University of Sydney will renovate its science buildings.

examples.note: Does not use 'the' where the organisation omits it.

parts.quote: Research at Charles Sturt University examined whether early Australian wheat varieties caused allergic reactions.

rules.quote: Always use lower case ‘the’ in body text.
rules.violation_condition: writing 'The' with an initial capital before an organisation name in running body text
when: Use 'The' with an initial capital only in emails and letters, or if the name appears in an alphabetical list arranged by 'The'.
If organisations omit the definite article from their name, do not use it in emails and letters.
rules.why: G-1, G-2, G-4: Single rule for handling 'the' in organisation names across body text vs letters/lists.

In all other cases for organisation names, don’t use possessive apostrophes.

rules.quote: Use an apostrophe only when it forms part of the official name of an organisation.

covers.quote: Use the singular verb with organisation names
This applies even if organisation names end in an ‘s’and look plural.

Woolworths are advertising their new stock.
